> 谷神不死，是謂玄牝。玄牝之門，是謂天地根。綿綿若存，用之不勤。

Chapter 5 said the hollow opens and closes like a bellows. Chapter 6 asks the obvious follow-up: why doesn't it run out?

The answer is given in two images, and both have been mistranslated into something smaller than they are.

## 谷: the valley

A valley is a depression between two mountains. It has no product of its own. Everything that grows in it grows because the slopes give it water, and the water collects because the ground is low.

谷 is the image of 虛而能受 — empty and therefore able to receive. Not passive emptiness, but the kind that gathers. The valley is not "nothing"; it is the shape that makes confluence possible.

## 神 is not a god

谷神 is routinely rendered "the spirit of the valley," which imports a deity the Chinese does not contain.

神 here is 申 — the character is a flash of lightning, the crooked line that appears and is gone. It names an unforeseeable generative potential inside the hollow: not a person, not a will, but the thing that keeps producing without being visible while it produces.

So 谷神不死 is not "the valley spirit is immortal." It is: the receiving-generating function does not die out. Which is why the next clause can name it 玄牝 without contradiction.

## 牝: not the female body

牝 is the receiving, bearing side — in animals, the female; in the pair 牡牝, the two ends of a cycle. 玄牝 is not a goddess and not a gendered image of nature.

It is the whole reciprocating mechanism: 牡 and 牝 as the two phases of one process, named together. Reading it as "the feminine" halves the image and loses the point — that giving and receiving are phases of the same function, not two substances.

## 不死 is not longevity

The chapter is not promising that anything lives forever. 不死 qualifies the function, not a being: the capacity to receive and generate does not exhaust itself.

> 綿綿若存，用之不勤.

綿綿 is continuous and fine, like a thread that never breaks. 若存 — as if it were there. 用之不勤 — use it and it is not worn out; 勤 here is exhaustion, not diligence.

That is the whole claim: the source is not depleted by use, because it is not a stock. It is a function of the hollow.

## What follows for practice

Two errors are common, and they are mirror images.

The first is treating rest as a stock you draw down: I have some energy, I spend it, I must refill. That model is accurate for muscles and misleading for attention. The thing that actually runs out is not capacity but the narrow channel you are forcing capacity through.

The second is treating the source as something to acquire. If it is 谷 — a shape, not a possession — then the work is to keep the shape: low enough to receive, open enough to let things collect.
